Most visitors eat in Dotonbori and fly home thinking that's Osaka. One stop from Osaka Station there's a 2.6 km covered street where the city actually eats, and almost nobody on a first trip finds it 👇

We didn't want to write another "top 10 things to do in Osaka" list. So we took our time with this one and checked every opening hour, closing day and price against official listings before putting it up.

🍣 WHAT LOCALS EAT

Harukoma is the oldest sushi shop on Tenjinbashisuji, and the queue tells you why: big, fresh pieces, with plates from around ¥100. It closes on Tuesdays. Go mid-afternoon and the line is shortest.

Butchers along the arcade fry croquettes at the counter for a few hundred yen. That's the walking snack here, more than takoyaki.

After six, the lanes north of JR Tenma fill with standing bars. One drink, two small plates, then the next bar. Nobody stays in one place, and that's the fun of it.

🚶 A SIMPLE HALF DAY

Start at Osaka Tenmangu Shrine at 10, walk north up the arcade snacking as you go, sushi for lunch, rest in the afternoon, and come back after dark. Tenma is at its best at night.

🛏️ WHERE TO SLEEP

Ogimachi side if you want to walk home from the bars. Tenjinbashisuji 6-chome if you want quiet mornings and an easy day trip to Kyoto.

📅 WORTH KNOWING

The Japan Mint's cherry blossom lane nearby opens for only about a week in mid-April, and you have to reserve online. That's also the week Osaka hotels get expensive.

If you only get one free evening in Osaka, we'd spend it here, not in the crowds.

Most visitors sleep in Namba and never see where Osaka actually lives. These two neighbourhoods are a short ride from the centre, with cheaper dinners, lantern-lit bars full of office workers, and quiet mornings 👇

📍 TENMA
1 stop from Osaka Station on the JR Loop Line

🛍️ Japan's longest covered shopping street runs right through it. Tenjinbashisuji is 2.6 km long, with about 600 shops selling croquettes, fish, pickles and old-school coffee.

🏮 Just north of JR Tenma are the Ura-Tenma alleys: tiny izakaya under hundreds of lanterns, about 5 minutes on foot.

🍻 It's lively at night, but local-lively. Office workers and neighbours, not tour groups.

🚇 Getting around: the JR Loop Line takes you to Osaka Station for Kyoto trains, the airport express and Universal Studios. The Sakaisuji Line reaches Nipponbashi in about 10 minutes.

📍 TSURUHASHI
Osaka's Korean neighbourhood

🥩 Famous for yakiniku. The market lanes start the moment you step out of the station.

🚶 Miyuki-dori Koreatown is a 10–15 minute walk south.

🦌 Kintetsu trains to Nara stop here, and the Sennichimae Line runs direct to Namba. A smart base if Nara is on your list.

✅ OUR TAKE

First trip, two or three nights? Stay central. It saves time.

Second trip, four nights or more, or going mainly for the food? Tenma or Tsuruhashi gives you everyday Osaka.

Hotel breakfast, or breakfast where Osaka's restaurant chefs buy their fish? On one morning of your trip, it's worth swapping. Here's a 300-year-old working market one subway stop from the centre, and exactly when to go 👇

Hotel breakfasts are comfortable, and on most mornings that's exactly what you want.

But you can have scrambled eggs anywhere in the world. This one you can only have in Osaka.

🏮 KIZU WHOLESALE MARKET

More than 300 years of history. Every morning, chefs from Osaka's restaurants come here for fish, vegetables and dried goods.

Visitors can walk in and buy too.

It's quieter and less polished than the famous markets. No crowds of tour groups, just a working market getting on with its day. That's exactly why we love it.

🚇 HOW TO GET THERE

Osaka Metro Midosuji or Yotsubashi Line to Daikokucho.

Take Exit 1. It's about 3 minutes on foot.

⏰ WHEN TO GO

Best between 8:30 and 10:30.

Stalls open around dawn for the chefs, and many close by late morning, so don't sleep in.

Closed Sundays, national holidays, some Wednesdays, and 31 Dec – 4 Jan. Check the calendar on kizu-ichiba.com the night before.

🍣 HOW WE'D SPEND THAT MORNING

1️⃣ Skip the buffet, just for this one day.

2️⃣ Ride the subway to Daikokucho.

3️⃣ Walk the aisles slowly and watch the market at work.

4️⃣ Sit down to a seafood bowl.

5️⃣ Head back into the city with the whole day ahead of you, and a breakfast you'll actually remember.

➕ TWO MORE LOCAL MARKETS

🥩 Tsuruhashi Market: covered lanes right outside Tsuruhashi Station, full of yakiniku, Korean grocers and fish stalls. Come hungry in the evening, and bring cash.

🛍️ Tenjinbashisuji: a 2.6 km covered shopping street locals use every day. About 40 minutes end to end, and lovely when it rains.

We priced the same three nights on both sides of Osaka Station. Walking 12 minutes saved ¥9,474. Here's when that walk is worth it, and when it isn't 👇

🤔 A or B? Pick one, then see what we found 👉 https://japanbystation.com/nakazakicho-vs-umeda-hotel

It's one of the most common Osaka booking questions: pay more to sleep right at the station, or walk a little and keep the money?

📅 Mon 14 – Thu 17 Dec 2026, 1 adult, Booking.com, checked 23 Nov.

💰 THE PRICES

🏨 Hotel Monterey Osaka, about 400 m from Osaka Station: ¥34,394 for 3 nights.

🌿 Quintessa Hotel Osaka Umeda, about 400 m from Nakazakicho Station, double room, rated 8.5: ¥24,920 for 3 nights.

That's about ¥3,160 a night less, or ¥9,474 over the stay.

🚶 THE CATCH

It's about 800 m, roughly 12 minutes on foot, from Osaka Station.

Add a few minutes to get from your platform to the street. Osaka Station is big, and first-timers often underestimate it.

Rather not walk? Nakazakicho is one stop from Higashi-Umeda on the Tanimachi subway line.

✅ OUR TAKE

👜 Small bag: walk it. You'll be walking to Umeda most days anyway.

🧳 Heavy suitcase: still book Nakazakicho, and take a taxi on arrival and departure only. Osaka taxis start at ¥600, the ride is about 6 minutes, so expect ¥600–800 each way. You still keep around ¥7,900.

🚄 Early trains most mornings: then the hotel on top of the station is worth it. Hotel Granvia Osaka is about 100 m from the platforms, but it was ¥49,243 for the same three nights.

📏 ONE RULE OF THUMB

Check the gap on your own dates. If it drops below about ¥500 a night, the two taxis cancel out the saving. Book in Umeda.

Booking an apartment for your group in Osaka? The city stopped accepting new special-zone rental applications on 29 May 2026 and is inspecting rentals more closely, so unlicensed listings can be cancelled at short notice. Here's the 3-step check we'd do before paying 👇

🤔 Guess first, then check the answer 👉 https://japanbystation.com/osaka-four-friends

⚠️ IS IT LEGAL?

Short-term rentals in Japan need a registration or a special-zone certification.

Legal hosts must record your passport at check-in.

✅ OUR 3-STEP CHECK

1️⃣ Find the registration or certification number on the listing. No number, no booking.

2️⃣ Expect a passport check. A host who never asks for ID is a warning sign.

3️⃣ Add cleaning fees and taxes for every night before you compare with hotel rooms.

🏠 PRIVATE APARTMENT

Good: one shared living space, a kitchen, a washing machine.

Watch: often one bathroom for four, cleaning fees, self check-in, and some have a minimum stay.

🏨 APARTMENT HOTEL

Good: real beds for four, a kitchenette, a laundry machine, and staff if something goes wrong.

Watch: popular with groups, so they book out early.

🛏️ TWO TWIN ROOMS

Good: two bathrooms, daily cleaning, easy cancellation, often right by the station.

Watch: rooms are compact, and there's no common space to hang out.

✅ OUR TAKE

Two or three nights: two twin rooms near a station are usually the easiest.

Four nights or more: an apartment hotel often wins, because laundry and a living room start to matter.

We priced the same three Tokyo nights at Ueno, Tokyo Station and Shinagawa before a bullet train to Kyoto. The cheapest saved about ¥40,000 and cost 13 minutes once 👇

🤔 A or B? Pick one, then see what we found 👉 https://japanbystation.com/narita-three-nights-then-shinkansen

Landing at Narita, three nights in Tokyo, then the Shinkansen? Where you sleep decides two journeys: the one in and the one out.

📅 Mon 14 – Thu 17 Dec 2026, 2 adults, Booking.com, checked 23 Nov.

1️⃣ UENO, OUR PICK FOR MOST TRIPS

🚆 The Skyliner runs from Narita to Keisei Ueno in as little as 41 minutes, for ¥2,470.

💰 Three nights for two from about ¥41,000, at well-rated hotels within 400 m.

🚄 Ueno to Kyoto took 2 h 28 min on our sample morning, with one change at Tokyo Station.

📍 Keisei Ueno and JR Ueno are separate stations, about 9 minutes apart on foot. Book on the Keisei side if you can.

2️⃣ TOKYO STATION, THE EASY LAST MORNING

🚆 The Narita Express reaches it in 53 minutes at its fastest, ¥3,140.

🚄 The 9:00 Nozomi reached Kyoto at 11:15, no change.

💸 But three nights started around ¥84,000, roughly double Ueno.

3️⃣ SHINAGAWA, FOR WEST-SIDE DAYS

🚆 The N'EX continues here: 71 minutes on our sample train, ¥3,330.

🚄 The same Nozomi stops 7 minutes after Tokyo, so it is 2 h 8 min to Kyoto.

🛍️ Shibuya is 13 minutes away on the Yamanote Line. Three nights from about ¥59,000.

✅ OUR TAKE

Ueno, for about 13 extra minutes on one morning. Shinagawa if two or more of your days are around Shibuya and Harajuku. Tokyo Station only with very heavy bags or a very early train.

There's something nice about a calm last morning before a long train ride. You don't need to pay double for it.

Landing at Haneda at 11 p.m.? On a weekday the last train toward Asakusa leaves Terminal 3 at 23:37, and the airport hotel cost the same as town on our date. Here's how we'd play it 👇

🚆 Quick quiz: which train is fastest? The answer 👉 https://japanbystation.com/haneda-late-arrival-first-night

📅 We checked Wed 16 Dec 2026, arriving at Terminal 3. After immigration and bags, we assume arrivals at about 23:45 at best.

🚆 THE LAST TRAINS

🏮 Asakusa: 23:37. Usually missed after a 23:00 landing.

🌆 Shinjuku and Shibuya: 23:51, changing at Shinagawa. Tight.

🚝 Hamamatsucho, Tokyo Station and Ueno: the Tokyo Monorail at 00:10.

A Hamamatsucho hotel is the safest central pick: the Monorail ends there at 00:26, no change.

🚕 NIGHT BUS OR TAXI

🚌 Late-night Limousine Buses leave at 0:20, 1:00, 1:40 and 2:20 for Shinjuku, Higashi-shinjuku and Ikebukuro, ¥2,800.

🚕 Fixed-fare taxis add 20% at night: about ¥9,800 to Shinjuku, plus tolls. Shared by two, roughly ¥5,000 each.

🏨 OR SLEEP AT THE AIRPORT

🛏️ Villa Fontaine Grand Haneda Airport is connected to Terminal 3 and has a 24-hour front desk. About ¥18,700 for two that night.

🏙️ Comparable central rooms were about ¥19,200–19,900 the same night.

🌅 First trains into the city leave at about 5:26.

✅ OUR TAKE

Checked bags and a 23:00 landing? Sleep at the airport on night one. Ride in the next morning in daylight, rested, with the whole day ahead.

Go straight in only with hand luggage and a Monorail-side hotel, or a hotel on the night-bus route.

Booking every Tokyo night by Tokyo Station "because the Shinkansen leaves from there"? On our dates that cost about double Ueno, to save 13 minutes on one morning 👇

📌 Save this for your trip (the full guide is here) 👉 https://japanbystation.com/narita-three-nights-then-shinkansen

It's one of the most common booking mistakes on Tokyo-then-Kyoto trips. It feels safe, but you pay for that safety on every single night, not just the last one.

❌ THE MISTAKE

🏨 Paying Tokyo Station prices for every night. On Mon 14 – Thu 17 Dec 2026, two adults, well-rated rooms within 700 m started around ¥84,000 for three nights.

⏱️ WHAT IT ACTUALLY SAVES

🚄 Tokyo Station to Kyoto by Nozomi: 2 h 15 min.

🚄 Ueno to Kyoto, with one change at Tokyo: 2 h 28 min.

🚄 Shinagawa to Kyoto, on the same Nozomi: 2 h 8 min. That's 7 minutes quicker than Tokyo Station.

✅ THE FIX

1️⃣ Sleep in Ueno for good-value nights: three nights from about ¥41,000 on the same dates.

2️⃣ Or Shinagawa if your days are on the west side. Shibuya is 13 minutes away.

3️⃣ Need a no-change, walk-to-the-platform morning with heavy bags or an early train? Move to Tokyo Station for the last night only, and keep the cheaper base for the rest.

💡 ONE MORE THING

Match your hotel to your airport train too. From Narita, the Skyliner reaches Keisei Ueno in as little as 41 minutes. The Narita Express goes to Tokyo Station and on to Shinagawa.

Big suitcase, Narita, hotel in Shinjuku: the train is about 30 minutes faster, but the bus can save you nearly 800 m of walking with your bags. Which would you take? 👇

🎯 Guess which option costs less, then check 👉 https://japanbystation.com/shinjuku-five-minutes-with-a-suitcase

🅰️ THE NARITA EXPRESS

⏱️ 87 minutes on our sample train, ¥3,330.

🚉 It arrives at platforms 5–6, and the lift route from there comes out at the south gates: New South, Koshu-kaido and Miraina Tower.

🏨 Great if your hotel is on the south side. Hotel Sunroute Plaza Shinjuku, for example, says 3 minutes from the South Exit.

📏 For a hotel on the north side, the walk from the south gates is about 970 m, before you count the station itself.

🅱️ THE LIMOUSINE BUS

⏱️ Narita to Tokyu Kabukicho Tower: 115 minutes on our sample timetable, ¥3,600.

💴 About 30 minutes slower and ¥270 more than the train.

📍 It drops you about 200 m from north-side hotels such as Hotel Gracery Shinjuku.

👨‍👩‍👧 Great with heavy bags, kids or tired legs after a long flight. Not so great if the next bus is an hour away.

💡 HOW WE DECIDE

1️⃣ Find which exit your hotel's "minutes" are counted from.

2️⃣ Hotel near the South Exit or Busta Shinjuku: take A.

3️⃣ North-side hotel, big case, and a bus within about 30 minutes: take B.

4️⃣ No bus soon: take A and budget 15–20 minutes from platform to reception.

🛗 One extra tip: Tokyo Metro's Marunouchi Line lifts from the East Gate up to Exits B11 and A6 run from 6:00 to 23:00. Late at night, expect stairs.

Asakusa has four stations with the same name. From Narita, the direct train stops at only one of them, and it is not the Tsukuba Express one most "near the station" hotels mean 👇

🎯 Guess which option costs less, then check 👉 https://japanbystation.com/asakusa-which-station-from-narita

🚆 WHERE YOUR AIRPORT TRAIN STOPS

✈️ Keisei's Access Express runs from Narita straight onto the Toei Asakusa Line. Our sample left Terminal 1 at 15:09 and reached Asakusa at 16:19, ¥1,380, no change.

🔁 To reach the Tsukuba Express Asakusa station instead, the fastest route we found needed two changes: 72 minutes and ¥3,010.

🧳 THE "NEAR ASAKUSA STATION" HOTEL

🏨 Hotel Trend Asakusa Annex lists itself as 3 minutes from the TX station. True: about 240 m from TX exit A1.

📏 But from the Toei station's step-free exit A2b it is about 670 m, around 9 minutes before you add suitcases.

💴 And on our dates it was not cheaper: ¥37,500 for 3 nights for 2 adults, against ¥36,845 at SORA Kaminarimon, about 250 m from exit A2b.

☀️ WHERE THE TX SIDE WINS

🎮 Akihabara in 5 minutes for ¥230, straight from the TX station.

🚇 Shibuya in 35 minutes for ¥260 from Tawaramachi on the Ginza Line, about 420 m away.

✅ OUR TAKE

With big bags, we'd book within about 300 m of the Toei station: you walk that 670 m on arrival day and again on departure day.

🎒 Travelling light and spending mornings in Akihabara? The TX side is a fine base.

We traced a hotel that says "5 minutes from Shinjuku Station" from the Narita Express platform. With a suitcase and the lifts, it was closer to 1 km. Here's why 👇

🗺️ Before you scroll on: the route and the map are here 👉 https://japanbystation.com/shinjuku-five-minutes-with-a-suitcase

The hotel: Hotel Gracery Shinjuku, which says 5 minutes from JR Shinjuku's East Exit. True, from that exit.

🚆 FROM THE NARITA EXPRESS

🕒 Our sample N'EX left Narita at 15:14 and reached Shinjuku at 16:41, for ¥3,330.

🚉 It stops at platforms 5–6. JR East says the lift route from there leads to the New South, Koshu-kaido and Miraina Tower gates, at the south end.

📏 The hotel is at the north end, about 970 m away on the street. With bags we budget 15–20 minutes to reception, which is on the 8th floor.

🚇 FROM THE ADVERTISED EXIT

🚶 From the JR East Exit plaza it really is about 470 m, around 6 minutes.

🛗 Step-free option: Tokyo Metro's Marunouchi Line has lifts from its East Gate to Exits B11 and A6, running 6:00–23:00 only. Exit B11 is about 450 m from the hotel.

🚌 FROM THE AIRPORT BUS

🎫 The Narita Limousine Bus runs straight to Tokyu Kabukicho Tower for ¥3,600.

⏳ It took 115 minutes on our sample timetable, about 30 minutes slower than the train.

📍 But the stop is only about 200 m from the hotel door.

✅ OUR TAKE

Always check which exit the "minutes" are counted from.

🧳 Big suitcase, north-side hotel: take the bus if one leaves within about 30 minutes of clearing customs. Otherwise take the N'EX and allow 15–20 minutes.

🚉 Hotel near the South Exit or Busta Shinjuku: the N'EX lift route ends right there, so the train wins.

Save this before you land at Narita with an Asakusa hotel booked: four quick checks that can save you a 670 m walk with your bags on arrival day, and again on the way back 👇

💴 The price gap surprised us. Take a guess, then look 👉 https://japanbystation.com/asakusa-which-station-from-narita

📋 THE CHECKLIST

1️⃣ Read the line name in your hotel's access notes. "Asakusa Station" can mean the Toei Asakusa Line, the Ginza Line, Tobu or the Tsukuba Express.

2️⃣ From Narita, ride the Access Express. It runs through to the Toei Asakusa Line: 70 minutes and ¥1,380 on our sample, with no change.

3️⃣ Use exit A2b if you need step-free access. A hotel next to SORA Kaminarimon is about 250 m away; one by the Tsukuba Express station is about 670 m.

4️⃣ Plan the way back too. On our sample departure the Access Express left Asakusa at 09:21 and reached Terminal 1 at 10:32, again from the Toei station.

💡 WHEN THE TSUKUBA EXPRESS SIDE MAKES SENSE

🎮 Akihabara mornings: 5 minutes and ¥230 from the TX station.

🎒 Light luggage, so the walk on arrival and departure day doesn't matter.

💴 A clearly lower price on your own dates, checked for the same nights and the same number of guests. On ours, 14–17 Dec 2026, the TX-side hotel we checked cost ¥655 more than one by the Toei station.

🏮 Get it right and your first Asakusa evening starts with a short walk to the lanterns, not a long one with a suitcase.

We priced three ways to sleep well after a late night in Shibuya on the same Wednesday. The quietest-sounding option was also the cheapest, by ¥5,245 👇

📌 Save this for your trip (the full guide is here) 👉 https://japanbystation.com/shibuya-nightlife-quiet-room

The setup: 2 adults, Wed 16 Dec 2026, a late bowl of ramen at ICHIRAN Shibuya (open 24 hours), then bed.

🏨 THE THREE OPTIONS

1️⃣ In the nightlife streets: Shibuya Tobu Hotel in Udagawacho, about 320 m from dinner, ¥29,045 for a small double.

🔎 We read about 150 recent reviews. One guest praised how well the room kept out street noise. The complaints were a room next to the lift and hearing the neighbours.

2️⃣ On a side street: Shibuya Granbell on the Sakuragaoka side, about 660 m and 9 minutes from dinner, ¥23,800 for a 20 m² double.

🌙 Reviews from 2024 to this month keep saying the same thing: a quiet street just behind the station.

3️⃣ One stop away: Prince Smart Inn Ebisu, ¥31,293 for a standard double.

🚃 The last Yamanote Line train left Shibuya at 00:48 that night. After that it is about 31 minutes on foot or roughly ¥1,300 on the taxi meter, before the late-night surcharge.

✅ OUR TAKE

We'd book the side street, not an upgrade. Quiet came from the street and from where your room sits on the corridor, not from paying more.

🕛 It changes if your nights end in Udagawacho after midnight. Then the 4-minute walk is worth it, and asking for a room away from the lift costs nothing.
